items.reason: Go validates and emits ordered initialItems notifications, stores codexResponseHandoffMode, and routes streamed assistant output from appserver turns into bounded realtime handoff_append itemAdded notifications. Commentary/final channels, final-message prefix, UTF-8-safe head/tail truncation, and client-managed/codexResponsesAsItems skips are covered.

Go rollout loading and doctor inventory now accept .jsonl.zst, map compressed siblings to canonical .jsonl state-DB keys, prefer plain rollouts, and report corrupt compressed files without false stale rows.

Rust codex exec consumes app-server notifications and conditionally backfills turn/completed items. Go exec runs the agent directly and emits completed items from the active AgentLoopResult, so there is no cross-thread notification/backfill stage to filter.
items.userImpact: Only the active direct exec result can produce Go exec completion items; background app-server thread notifications are not part of this execution path and cannot pollute stdout.

items.reason: Go TUI startup receives locally prepared model metadata and permission requirements; it has no equivalent pair of remote model/list and configRequirements/read requests to parallelize. This is an architecture difference, not an unimplemented Go request scheduler.
items.userImpact: No additional startup round trips are introduced in the Go path; model and permission data are already available locally or from the existing settings load.

items.reason: Go detects external project Markdown memory, verifies SHA-256 content, imports under extension-scoped resources with scope.json and source/project/cwd/hash metadata, rejects path/hash failures, and removes resources for disappeared projects without inventing rollout provenance.
The Rust crate removal is repository-structure cleanup, not a wire-protocol removal.
items.userImpact: Go retains its existing realtime capability; external protocol behavior is unchanged.

items.reason: Linux Landlock/bwrap is verified on a native Kali runner. Go now has a parameterized macOS seatbelt backend with workspace metadata protection, network restriction, Unix-socket allowlists, and CODEX_SANDBOX propagation; Darwin packages cross-compile. Native macOS seatbelt/root/desktop artifacts are still required.
